annotation.label: Signed history product with current and recent inputs
annotation.prospective_contrast: At fixed u=0.3 and h=0.5, contrast histories [1,0,0,0] and [0,0,0,1], then repeat at h=1.5. Their measured means differ by about 0.301 at h=0.5 and 0.190 at h=1.5; the endpoint history term alone cannot explain this, motivating tests of earlier versus later history contributions.
annotation.refutation_condition: Refit on fit only; reject if raw dev RMSE exceeds 0.06 or if frozen predictions miss either fresh intervention-pair mean by more than the 0.06 criterion.
annotation.scientific_change: Replace the failed u,h-only response with explicit dependence on the oldest interval and a nonlinear interaction of the interior history intervals, while retaining u and h.

annotation.label: History shape with waiting-time modulation
annotation.prospective_contrast: At u=0.65, compare the same histories [1,0,0,0] and [0,0,0,1] at h=0.5 versus h=2.2: the observed endpoint-history contrast changes from roughly 0.292 to 0.135. The model predicts only an h main effect, so acquire a new matched pair with mixed-sign histories at both waiting times to test for h-by-history interaction.
annotation.refutation_condition: The proposal is inadequate if fit-only refitting gives dev RMSE above 0.06 or frozen predictions fail the new mixed-sign pair contrasts beyond 0.06 response units.
annotation.scientific_change: Test the parsimonious additive history account first; the waiting-time dependence of the observed history contrast motivates a later interaction extension if this account fails.

annotation.label: Endpoint history with waiting-time modulation
annotation.prospective_contrast: At fixed u, compare histories that vary only history[3], including both active pairs and new held-out values of u and h. Also compare oldest-interval and newest-interval pulses across h to test whether the h-by-history effect is shared or interval-specific.
annotation.refutation_condition: Reject this representation if a fit-only refit has raw dev RMSE above 0.06 or misses any fresh hidden, random confirmation, or intervention-pair target by more than the stated RMSE criterion. A failure of this finite feature set does not refute history[3] dependence generally.
annotation.scientific_change: Replace the failed u,h-only response with a quadratic response in current drive, waiting time, and explicitly indexed oldest and newest history intervals. The active interventions preserve a large newest-interval effect; the fresh and observed contrasts motivate testing waiting-time modulation rather than treating the fitted C0 coefficients as supported.

annotation.label: Explicit endpoint and interior history response
annotation.prospective_contrast: At matched u and h, compare histories with the same oldest and newest entries but different interior entries, alongside a newest-entry flip. Repeat at two h values to assess whether the combined history contribution changes with waiting time.
annotation.refutation_condition: Reject if fit-only refitting exceeds 0.06 raw dev RMSE or fails a frozen prediction target on fresh conditions or either acquired active pair under the specified criterion. This would refute this chosen feature combination, not all nonlinear interior-history effects.
annotation.scientific_change: Retain explicit oldest and newest interval contributions and add the proposed nonlinear interior-history product, with quadratic interactions allowing waiting time to modulate history effects. The acquired contrasts reject C1/C2's executable u-only fits; they do not establish the product term itself, so this remains a testable revision rather than an accepted law.
